answer: Timed Arrival Pearl Accrual. Each agent identity must accumulate a pearl (a slow, fixed-rate reputation credit) that only matures after sustained, irregular arrival patterns; sudden bursts are discounted by a prism check that splits traffic across time windows and scores each slice separately. The tide of accumulated credit must rise steadily for an identity to transact at full weight. An attacker running many fake identities pays the full wall-clock maturation delay per identity, so creating N sybils costs N times the minimum aging period, making mass fabrication slow and expensive.
